I've been farming these fields for over forty years now, and at sixty-nine I don't try to be clever anymore. My land is about eight mu, and I stick with what I know: wheat and maize in the double-cropping system. The winter wheat went in last October — I sowed Jimai 22, a reliable improved variety I've used for years and saved seed from when I could. Now that it's greening up, I'll irrigate three times total if the rain doesn't come: once in early spring to wake it up, again at jointing stage, and a third time at grain filling. I put down compound fertilizer as basal before sowing, and I'll topdress with urea when the wheat starts growing fast. The extension technician says fifteen kilograms of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I usually apply about sixteen — I'd rather spend a few extra yuan than risk a bad yield if the weather turns dry. For phosphorus and potassium I don't go overboard; the soil here is decent, so five and four kilograms per mu are enough. I'll spray twice for weeds and rust. After harvest in early June, the window is tight — barely a week — so I'll plant Denghai 605 hybrid maize right into the stubble without tilling. The maize is less fussy; I'll irrigate twice, spray for borers and weeds twice, and topdress nitrogen once. I thought about cotton, but my back isn't what it used to be, and machine-harvesting wheat and maize saves my strength. If the weather cooperates, I expect about 450 kg per mu of wheat and 500 kg per mu of maize.
